A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of SMARLI, with identifiable corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. However, v2 refers to unavailable supplementary Janus-Pro results, OverLayBench Simple/Regular results, and tokenizer/weight ablations, limiting verification of those additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMARLI results on LayoutSAM-Eval, masking and reward ablations in Tables 1–3, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original SMARLI evaluations on LayoutSAM-Eval, OverLayBench-Complex and T2I-CompBench, together with masking and reward ablations in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The layout reward changes substantially: v1 averages cropped-region CLIP similarities, whereas v2 combines VLM-based binary VQA scores with Grounding DINO mIoU and precision scores. This introduces new reward components targeting semantic consistency, localization and false positives. The tokenizer, structured masking and stepwise GRPO trajectory replay remain substantially the same; their expanded explanations do not establish additional algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained LayoutSAM training data and LayoutSAM-Eval evaluation, v2 adds OverLayBench-Complex for densely overlapping layouts and T2I-CompBench for compositional generation, including numeracy and spatial reasoning. These broaden the evaluated input conditions and task requirements. Simple/Regular OverLayBench results are referenced but not supplied.

E2.justification: In the corresponding LayoutSAM-Eval comparison, v2 removes Ranni and Be Yourself and adds PlanGen, InstanceAssemble and SiamLayout-FLUX. The original SiamLayout comparator is retained as SiamLay-SD3. Additional reported comparisons include EliGen on OverLayBench and SDXL, PixArt-alpha, DALL-E 3 and Show-o on T2I-CompBench. PlanGen adds a direct autoregressive competitor absent from v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds Grounding DINO filtering requiring training-sample mIoU and precision above 0.9, increases the within-box layout-advantage weight from 1.1 to 1.2, and evaluates detection metrics on 895 selected LayoutSAM-Eval samples. It removes IS reporting and introduces OverLayBench-specific metrics and GPT-5.2-generated layouts for T2I-CompBench. The principal SFT and GRPO iteration counts, batch sizes and learning rates remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's HPS-versus-CLIP-layout ablation is replaced by an expanded analysis separating HPS, VQA and detection rewards. v2 Table 5 and Figure 6 test whether semantic rewards miss localization/false-positive errors and whether detection rewards sacrifice attribute fidelity. The retained masking ablation gains detection metrics and qualitative failure examples in Figure 5. Referenced supplementary tokenizer and weight studies cannot be inspected.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates. The unchanged GRPO group size of four describes training rollouts, not repeated experimental trials.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces SMARLI's spatial/IR values of 95.33/69.08 with 95.55/74.81 under revised reward and training settings; FID remains 18.16. These are not controlled same-setting gains. New benchmark tables and revised reward ablations add substantial results, while the original masking-ablation values are retained. The expanded comparison also changes rankings: SiamLay-FLUX leads spatial accuracy and PlanGen leads FID in v2.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 4 defines a new weighted VQA/mIoU/precision reward, replacing v1's prose definition of average regional CLIP similarity. This is a limited mathematical-definition change. The GRPO objective, tokenizer equations and overall advantage combination are otherwise retained, with no new theorem, proof or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's claim to be the first layout-conditioned AR text-to-image framework. Its abstract and introduction add claims of transfer to standard next-token models and exposure-bias mitigation, while the contributions emphasize validation across multiple benchmarks. These materially revise novelty and applicability claims beyond the retained structured-masking and quality/layout-control contributions.

C2.justification: The main interpretation of masking and the quality/layout tradeoff remains. v2 adds explanations for exposure-bias mitigation, global-prompt disambiguation of overlaps, and complementary reward weaknesses: VQA can overlook inaccurate boundaries and false positives, while detection can neglect detailed semantics. It removes v1's speculation that a stronger AR backbone could close the image-quality gap.

D1.justification: v2 discloses SFT runtime of three days on eight MI300X GPUs, GRPO runtime of four hours on eight MI250 GPUs, reward coefficients, and which baseline results were imported or reproduced. Conversely, v1's approximately one-million-sample SFT disclosure and Qwen3-14B redundancy-filter identification disappear. Their omission reduces documentation and does not establish a change to the SFT sample count.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions SMARLI relative to PlanGen, explicitly acknowledging an existing AR layout-generation approach and motivating improvements to interference and image quality. It adds discussion of InstanceAssemble and literature supporting the new rewards and benchmarks. The earlier TwFA/LayoutEnc discussion and citations disappear. This changes the novelty argument, not merely bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Preliminary material moves inside Method, masking is organized around named principles, and experiments are divided into separate layout-to-image and text-to-image evaluations. Front matter also changes, including an additional author and affiliation, keywords and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 1 moves before the abstract with refreshed examples; Figure 2 changes its reward diagram; and Figure 3 revises the comparison grid. New overlap and ablation figures are added. Tables gain parameter counts and detection metrics, and the reward table separates VQA and detection components. The original ablation tables are matched despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's single-benchmark, diffusion-only comparison: it adds a direct AR competitor, challenging overlapping-layout evaluation, and spatial metrics and reward-component controls that examine concrete failure modes. Its novelty positioning is also more qualified. These gains materially improve support for the central layout-control claims, rather than merely raising reported scores. Missing supplementary evidence, removed IS reporting and reduced training-data disclosure remain limitations, but do not outweigh the stronger main-paper validation.
